title: Number the scale notes
summary: Count from the tonic, starting at one.

steps.title: Number the scale notes
steps.body:
**scale degree** means the number of a note in a scale. In G major, G is 1, A is 2, B is 3, C is 4, D is 5, E is 6 and F# is 7. The next G returns to 1.

**Why it matters:** Numbers describe a note’s job even when the key changes.

steps.title: See it on the fretboard
steps.body: Start at G2 on string 6 fret 3 and follow the lit notes upward. The number belongs to the sound in the key, not the fret or string number.

items.prompt: Play D3, scale degree 5 in G major.

steps.title: Explore the sounds
steps.body: Find G in two places. Both are degree 1 in G major even though their fret positions differ.
